sections.html:
Greeley is the county seat of Weld County and its largest municipality, about 49 miles north-northeast of the State Capitol in Denver. The Cache la Poudre River crosses the north side, and open farmland lines the edges of town. A house near a river corridor and one on the farmland fringe face different conditions, and buyers will ask about both.

The oldest blocks near the center date to the nineteenth century, when telephones and electric lights arrived early. A traditional buyer's inspection of a house that old can bring repair requests for wiring, plumbing and structure. A cash buyer who purchases as-is does not make you fix those items first.

Students and staff at the University of Northern Colorado, which enrolls about 9,000, keep rental demand active, so landlords are a large share of local sellers. Households tied to the city's big employers sometimes have to move quickly after a transfer or layoff, and for them the closing date outweighs the last bit of price.

Hail is the big roof worry. The farmland around Greeley sees roughly 7 to 9 hail days a year, and on May 28, 2024 a severe storm hit the east side, burying some areas under more than a foot of hail. The mayor signed a local disaster declaration, and officials put damage to city property above $1.45 million.

If your roof was hit and you never filed or finished an insurance claim, expect it to come up. A retail buyer's inspector will flag it, and a lender may require repairs. Cash buyers fold the roof's condition into the price instead of asking for a replacement.

  • Ask your insurer whether a hail claim is still open or can still be filed.
  • Keep invoices for any roof, gutter or window work already done.
  • Photograph damage you have not repaired before you list or request an offer.

Summers run hot, with highs usually in the 90s, and winters are cold and dry, so exteriors take a beating from both ends of the year.

sections.h2: Weld County property tax due dates
sections.html:
Payment optionDue date
First halfFebruary 28
Second halfJune 15
Full paymentApril 30

Weld County bills in arrears, so the tax you pay in a given year covers the prior year. Notices usually go out before the end of January to the owner of record. Partial payments are not accepted, and a bill of $25 or less must be paid in one payment. A late postmark brings interest that starts at 1 percent in March for a first half and rises month by month.

Your mortgage company does not get a copy of the notice from the treasurer. When a lender pays from escrow and you also pay, the treasurer processes the lender's payment and returns yours. The treasurer's office has a request form for a Certificate of Taxes Due, the document a closing uses to show what the parcel owes.

The assessor changes the owner's name only after the deed is recorded with the Weld County Clerk and Recorder. As the seller, make sure the closing company records promptly, so the next tax notice goes to the new owner and not to you.

sections.h2: Where a Greeley sale loses time
sections.html:
Every Colorado sale follows the same basic path. A cash purchase just removes several steps.

  • Listing with an agent adds weeks for photos, showings, offers, the buyer's inspection and the appraisal.
  • Financed buyers can fall through when an appraisal comes in low or underwriting stalls.
  • A cash purchase can skip the appraisal and loan approval, so closing can be set around your move date.
  • Either way, a title company handles the deed, the tax certificate and the recording with Weld County.

We buy Greeley houses in whatever shape they are in, including hail-damaged roofs, tenants, deferred maintenance and open probate paperwork. The decision is yours, and an offer carries no obligation.

Storm damage, older plumbing and electrical, tenants in place and inherited property come up most often. Each one slows a retail listing.

  • Roof and exterior wear from hail seasons.
  • Rentals with tenants in place and deferred upkeep.
  • Estates where heirs live out of state and want one closing instead of months of upkeep.
  • Owners relocating for work after a change at a large local employer.

If yours looks like one of these, tell us about the property. You will get a straightforward offer or a clear reason we cannot make one.

An owner who wants out of a rental can sell with the tenant in place or without. Share the lease terms and the monthly rent, and the offer will account for the tenancy. You do not have to empty the house or finish repairs first. If the tenants plan to stay, a buyer who intends to keep renting may value the income. If they plan to leave, tell the buyer the move-out date so the closing can be timed around it.

On closing day the title company confirms the numbers, subtracts taxes and any loan payoff, and pays you the balance. It also files the deed with the county. Bring identification and the keys, and expect a short appointment. Because no lender is involved, nobody is waiting on final loan paperwork, so signing day is usually calm. Ask the title company when the funds will reach you, so you can plan the move around the payout.

Have a few items ready and the first call goes faster. Pull the latest Weld County tax notice, since a bill that was paid or is still open changes the closing math. Note whether the roof, gutters or windows have been repaired and keep the invoices. If heirs share ownership, line up who can sign. If a lender holds a mortgage, request a payoff statement.

The offer depends on what the buyer learns about the house, so be candid about problems. Hiding a leak or an unfinished claim only slows the deal later, when the title work and a walkthrough would surface it anyway.

Estates add a layer. Until the probate paperwork authorizes someone to sell, nobody can pass a clear deed, so confirm who holds that authority before you request an offer. After that, the process matches any other sale: title work, the tax certificate, signing and recording. Heirs who live out of state often prefer one closing over months of upkeep, taxes and utilities on a house nobody lives in.

faqs.a: Yes. Greeley is the county seat and most populous municipality in Weld County, so deeds are recorded with the Weld County Clerk and Recorder and property tax is billed by the Weld County Treasurer.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Greeley?
faqs.a: The first half is due February 28, the second half June 15, and a single full payment April 30. Late postmarks add interest, so check with the treasurer for the current year.

faqs.q: Does hail damage hurt my chances of selling a Greeley house?
faqs.a: It can, because inspectors and lenders flag damaged roofs. The area sees several hail days a year, and a major storm in May 2024 hit the east side hard. A cash buyer can account for the roof in the offer instead of asking you to repair it first.

faqs.q: What document shows the taxes owed at closing?
faqs.a: A Certificate of Taxes Due. The Weld County Treasurer has a request form for it, and your title company normally orders it.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Greeley house with tenants living in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us about the lease and the rent, and the offer will include the tenancy. You do not need to empty the house or finish repairs first.
